correctness.rationale: All assumptions r>=2 and n_i>=2 are explicit. For each nonempty skew fort W, if the hub is absent each occupied blade must have at least three white vertices, while if the hub is present every blade must contain at least two white vertices. These exhaust the minimal forts. Forcing sets are exactly complements avoiding those two fort types; this gives the product-minus-correction polynomial. Both minimal-profile cases have N-2r blue vertices, with counts shown by direct labeled choices; maximal failing sets arise from minimal forts of size three, except the all-triangle case. Direct exhaustive adjacency-rule simulation on 182 parameter profiles agreed on all 1,291,680 initial subsets, while 71,009 candidate white subsets were examined for minimal forts. The infinite theorem rests on the structural proof, not these finite tests.

The known odd-cycle bouquet regime with every peripheral clique of size two is acknowledged rather than asserted as novel. Publicly indexed related studies of ordinary zero forcing and dissociation use different definitions and do not imply the skew forcing enumeration or constant span without further mathematical arguments. value.rationale: Skew zero forcing is a natural graph-propagation and inverse-eigenvalue invariant. The complete heterogeneous clique-bouquet polynomial determines every cardinality count, not only a numerical minimum; the exact minimal-fort hypergraph has both local triple obstructions and a global hub-transversal obstruction. The resulting skew forcing span is unexpectedly independent of clique sizes whenever one blade exceeds a triangle, depending only on r as 2r-2. The theorem also proves all inclusion-minimal forcing sets are minimum, and counts all of them. This fills an explicit gap between prior odd-cycle-bouquet zero-span results and general skew closure theory. The all-triangle case is prior-covered and acknowledged, not used as the sole value claim.
